formation.title: The Kingdom Restored
formation.text:
Jerusalem is ours. The Holy City, over which so many have fought and died, has been taken under the banner of the Cross. Pilgrims weep at the sight of the Holy Sepulchre, knights kneel in prayer upon the Temple Mount, and merchants eye the bustling ports of Acre and Tyre with barely concealed avarice. The Kingdom of Jerusalem is proclaimed anew, but what manner of kingdom shall it be? Shall we be a fortress of the faith, a militant state dedicated to the defense of Christendom's holiest sites? Or shall we embrace our position at the crossroads of three continents, growing rich on the trade that flows through our ports and caravansaries?

This choice unlocks a destiny path in the Traditions tab.

options.text: We are the Sword and Shield of Christ!

modifiers.name: Defender of the Faith
modifiers.text: The Kingdom of Jerusalem stands as the shield of Christendom in the East, a bulwark against the infidel sustained by the faith and swords of its knights.

options.text: Let the riches of East and West flow through our hands.

modifiers.name: Crossroads of Commerce
modifiers.text: The ports and markets of the Holy Land channel the riches of East and West, making Jerusalem the pivot upon which Mediterranean commerce turns.

advances.name: Feudal Outremer
advances.text: The Frankish settlers established a feudal administration adapted to the realities of governing a narrow coastal kingdom surrounded by hostile powers, blending Western custom with local practice.

advances.name: Arriere-Ban of Outremer
advances.text: Unlike in Europe where feudal service was limited to forty days, the Kings of Jerusalem demanded a full year of military service from their vassals, a necessity born of constant existential threat.

advances.name: Turcopole Tradition
advances.text: The Turcopoles were locally recruited light cavalry who served as scouts, mounted archers, and skirmishers. Often drawn from Christianized Seljuks or Syrian Christians, they comprised up to half of the kingdom's mounted forces.

advances.name: Pilgrim Roads
advances.text: The protection and taxation of pilgrims traveling to the holy sites formed a major source of income for the kingdom, with Jerusalem's population doubling during the summer pilgrimage season.

advances.name: Sugar Estates of the Levant
advances.text:
The Crusaders found sugarcane already under cultivation in the Levant and expanded its production dramatically. Most sugar consumed in thirteenth-century Europe originated from the Crusader states.

Available in: Sugar Press

advances.name: Concentric Fortification
advances.text: The concentric castle, with its multiple rings of curtain walls and interlocking fields of fire, was perfected in the Crusader states as a response to the advanced siege techniques of their Muslim adversaries.

event.title: The Concentric Fortress
event.text: Our engineers have perfected a revolutionary approach to fortification. Drawing on the bitter lessons of siege warfare against Saracen sappers and siege engines, they have developed the concentric castle, multiple rings of curtain walls, each commanding the one before it, with towers positioned for interlocking fields of fire. The inner walls rise above the outer, so that defenders can shoot over their comrades below. Bent entrances, murder holes, and machicolations turn every approach into a killing ground. Krak des Chevaliers, Belvoir, and Margat stand as monuments to this new art of defense. Shall we continue to invest in these mighty fortresses?

options.text: Build walls that will stand until Judgment Day.

modifiers.name: Walls of Outremer
modifiers.text: The great concentric fortresses of the Holy Land represent the pinnacle of defensive architecture, their layered walls and killing grounds a lesson in stone.

options.text: These walls shall break any siege.

modifiers.name: Castle Doctrine
modifiers.text: The concentric fortresses of Outremer are more than mere walls; they are a doctrine of defense, a system of strongpoints that makes the kingdom nearly impregnable.

advances.name: Acre Entrepot
advances.text: Acre replaced Alexandria as the most important trading port in the eastern Mediterranean, welcoming traders from Byzantium, North Africa, Arabia, and the Italian maritime republics.

advances.name: Italian Quarter
advances.text: The Italian maritime republics, Venice, Genoa, and Pisa, maintained autonomous trading quarters in the ports of Outremer, their financial resources and naval strength essential to the kingdom's survival.

advances.name: Templar Banking
advances.text: The Knights Templar developed an early system of banking and credit, allowing pilgrims to deposit funds in Europe and withdraw them in the Holy Land, a financial innovation born of practical necessity.

advances.name: Assizes of Jerusalem
advances.text: The Assizes of Jerusalem constituted the most comprehensive feudal legal code of the medieval period, governing everything from land tenure and feudal obligation to commercial regulation and burgess rights.

event.title: The Assizes of Jerusalem
event.text: The jurists of the realm have completed the great work of codification. Drawing upon the customs of the Frankish settlers, the traditions of the Italian communes, and the practical necessities of ruling a diverse kingdom in hostile lands, they have compiled the Assizes of Jerusalem, the most comprehensive legal code in Christendom east of Constantinople. The Haute Cour and the Cour des Bourgeois now have clear written precedent to guide their deliberations, from matters of feudal obligation and land tenure to the regulation of commerce and the rights of the burgesses. Shall we strengthen the crown's hand through this new legal instrument, or use it to stabilize the realm?

options.text: The law is the foundation of good government.

modifiers.name: Legacy of the Assizes
modifiers.text: The codification of the Assizes of Jerusalem provides a comprehensive legal framework that governs the affairs of Outremer with wisdom and precedent.

modifiers.name: Outremer Settlement
modifiers.text: Good laws and just governance attract settlers to the Holy Land, building a stable population base that sustains the kingdom through colonization rather than conquest alone.

advances.name: Navy of Outremer
advances.text: Though dependent on Italian naval power, the Kingdom of Jerusalem maintained its own fleet of war galleys to patrol the Levantine coast, protect merchant shipping, and support amphibious operations.

advances.name: Holy Land Relics
advances.text: The trade in holy relics, souvenirs, and religious artifacts was a lucrative industry in the Crusader states, feeding the insatiable appetite of European Christendom for tangible connections to sacred sites. Carvers work olive wood and mother of pearl into rosaries and crosses for the pilgrims to carry home.

advances.name: Desert Warfare
advances.text: Generations of warfare against the Ayyubids and Mamluks taught the Crusaders to adapt their tactics to the arid terrain of the Levant, learning to manage water supplies, avoid ambushes, and fight in the scorching heat.

advances.name: Hospitaller Medicine
advances.text: The Knights Hospitaller maintained the great Hospital of St. John in Jerusalem, where physicians drawing on both European and Arabic medical traditions treated the sick and wounded regardless of religion or rank.

advances.name: Crossroads Diplomacy
advances.text: Positioned at the junction of three continents, the Kingdom of Jerusalem maintained complex diplomatic relationships with Byzantium, the Italian republics, the Papacy, and at times even their Muslim neighbors.

advances.name: Frankish Chivalry
advances.text: The Frankish heavy cavalry charge was the most feared weapon in the Crusader arsenal, armored knights on destriers smashing into enemy formations with the momentum of an avalanche of iron.

advances.name: Levantine Commerce
advances.text: By the later period of the kingdom, commercial income had eclipsed feudal rents as the primary source of royal revenue, with the ports of Acre and Tyre serving as vital conduits for East-West trade.

advances.name: Holy Land Garrison
advances.text: The permanent garrison system of the Crusader states, maintained through the military orders and feudal obligations, allowed a small Christian population to hold vast territories against numerically superior foes.

advances.name: Crusader Legacy
advances.text: The legacy of the Crusader Kingdom endures, in the great castles that still stand, in the legal traditions that influenced European jurisprudence, and in the cultural exchange between East and West that it facilitated.

advances.name: Kingdom Restored
advances.text: The Kingdom of Jerusalem rises again in a new age, its ancient claim to the Holy City given new life and new purpose.

advances.name: Eastern Diplomacy
advances.text: Navigating the complex web of alliances and rivalries in the modern Middle East requires the same diplomatic skill that once sustained a narrow strip of Christian territory amid a sea of Muslim powers.

advances.name: Holy City Renown
advances.text: Jerusalem is a city sacred to three faiths, and its ruler holds a position of unmatched cultural and religious significance, commanding the attention and respect of the entire world.

advances.name: Gardens of Jaffa
advances.text: The plain behind Jaffa is planted with orange, lemon and pomegranate, each grove watered from its own well by a wheel that a mule turns. Twice in this age the town is sacked, and twice the gardens are planted again.

destiny.name: Destiny of Jerusalem
destiny.text: The Kingdom of Jerusalem has been restored. Now it must choose its destiny, to crusade for the faith or to build an empire of trade.

event.title: The Destiny of Jerusalem
event.text: The Crown of Jerusalem sits upon a brow that bears the weight of prophecy. We have restored the Kingdom, but which kingdom shall we build? The choices made at our founding echo forward into history, and now the path unfolds before us. Whether as defenders of the faith or masters of commerce, we shall carve our destiny into the stone of ages.

destiny.name: The Crusader States
destiny.text: The historic Crusader States are reunited under one crown. Antioch and the County of Tripoli are secured, and Kerak beyond the Jordan, the castle of the old lordship of Oultrejourdain, is held again, to forge a unified Christian front in the Levant.

conditions.text: Own Antioch, or a subject owns it
Own Tripoli, or a subject owns it
Own Al-Karak, or a subject owns it

event.title: The Crusader States Reunited
event.text: The banners of Antioch and Tripoli fly beside the Cross of Jerusalem once more. For the first time since the days of the early Crusades, the Christian states of the Levant stand united under a single crown. The Principality of Antioch, founded by Bohemond, and the County of Tripoli, carved out by Raymond of Toulouse, have been brought back into the fold. What was shattered by Muslim reconquest and Frankish division has been made whole again.

options.text: The Franks of Outremer are one people once more.

destiny.name: March to the East
destiny.text: The Cross is carried into the heartlands of Islam. The great cities of Damascus, Homs and Aleppo must fall to complete the Crusader dominion over Syria.

conditions.text: Own Damascus, or a subject owns it
Own Aleppo, or a subject owns it
Own Homs, or a subject owns it

event.title: The March to the East
event.text: Damascus has fallen. Aleppo has fallen. The great Muslim cities of Syria, which resisted a century of Crusader ambition, now bow to the Cross of Jerusalem. Saladin himself failed to hold what we have taken, and the Atabeg's domain lies shattered. The question now is how we wield this unprecedented power. Do we press forward as the hammer of God, driving ever deeper into the lands of the infidel? Or do we consolidate, building a lasting peace in the lands we have already won?

options.text: We are the hammer of God. Let none stand.

modifiers.name: Hammer of God
modifiers.text: The armies of Jerusalem march without rest, an unstoppable instrument of divine wrath. Yet ceaseless campaigning wears upon the spirit of the realm.

options.text: Build the peace of Jerusalem over all Syria.

modifiers.name: Pax Hierosolymitana
modifiers.text: The Peace of Jerusalem extends over all Syria. Conquered peoples are brought into the fold through fair governance and patient integration.

destiny.name: The New Crusade
destiny.text: The ultimate crusade is launched, southward to Cairo and onward to Mecca and Medina, the holy cities of Arabia. No Christian king has ever achieved what is now attempted.

conditions.text: Own Cairo, or a subject owns it
Own Mecca, or a subject owns it
Own Madīna, or a subject owns it

event.title: The New Crusade Triumphant
event.text: Cairo has fallen to the Cross. The holy cities of Arabia lie under our protection. What no Crusade has ever achieved, what Richard the Lionheart only dreamed of, has been accomplished. The Ayyubid heartland, the Mamluk stronghold, the sacred cities of Islam itself, all answer to the Crown of Jerusalem. The world watches in astonishment. Shall we be remembered as the Sword of Christ, the invincible warriors who conquered the East? Or as the architects of a new Kingdom of Heaven, a realm where the sacred legacy of the Holy Land transforms all it touches?

options.text: We are the Sword of Christ, and none may resist.

modifiers.name: Sword of Christ
modifiers.text: The Kingdom of Jerusalem wields the mightiest army in Christendom, though the upkeep of its far-flung fortresses strains the treasury.

options.text: We shall build a Kingdom of Heaven on earth.

modifiers.name: Kingdom of Heaven
modifiers.text: A realm of harmony and splendor where the sacred legacy of the Holy Land inspires artistic achievement and social stability.

destiny.name: Levantine Ports
destiny.text: Secure the great trading ports of the eastern Mediterranean. Cyprus and Beirut are the keys to controlling the Levantine sea lanes.

conditions.text: Own Famagusta, or a subject owns it
Own Beirut, or a subject owns it

event.title: The Levantine Ports Secured
event.text: Famagusta and Beirut, the twin jewels of the eastern Mediterranean, now fly the banner of Jerusalem. With Cyprus under our control, no ship crosses the Levantine Sea without our leave. Beirut's ancient harbor, once the pride of Phoenicia, now channels the wealth of three continents through Crusader hands. The Italian merchants who once held us hostage with their fleets now come as supplicants, begging for berths in our overflowing harbors.

options.text: The sea lanes of the Levant are ours.

destiny.name: The Western Silk Road
destiny.text: Draw the riches of the East through your markets. Silk and incense must flow through Crusader hands, making Jerusalem the western terminus of the great trade routes.

conditions.text: A market the country is in

children.text: Silk is produced in the market
Silk is traded in the market

conditions.text: A market the country is in

children.text: Incense is produced in the market
Incense is traded in the market

event.title: The Western Silk Road
event.text: Silk from Cathay, incense from Arabia, spices from India, all flow through the markets of the Holy Land. We have become what Venice and Genoa only aspired to be: the true middlemen between East and West. Our caravansaries overflow with goods, our counting houses ring with the clink of gold, and our factors sit in every port from Cyprus to Constantinople. Shall we press further into the caravan routes, becoming the lords of overland trade? Or shall we build a network of agents and factors, controlling commerce through knowledge and connections rather than territory?

options.text: Control the caravans and we control the East.

modifiers.name: Lords of the Caravans
modifiers.text: The overland trade routes of the East pass through Crusader hands, bringing silks and luxuries to the markets of the Holy Land.

options.text: Our agents shall know every market secret.

modifiers.name: Kings of the Counting House
modifiers.text: A vast network of agents and factors gives the kingdom unmatched commercial intelligence, though agricultural development suffers from neglect.

destiny.name: Emporium of Three Continents
destiny.text: Build a commercial empire spanning from Alexandria to Constantinople, and set a Court of the Chain or a merchants quarter in Alexandria so that the crown counts and taxes every cargo landed there. Control the crossroads where Europe, Asia, and Africa meet.

conditions.text: Own Alexandria, or a subject owns it
Own Constantinople, or a subject owns it
We own Alexandria and a Court of the Chain, Merchants Quarters, Grand Marketplace or Commerce Center stands there

event.title: Emporium of Three Continents
event.text: Alexandria and Constantinople, the two greatest commercial cities of the ancient world, now answer to the Crown of Jerusalem. We sit at the crossroads where Europe, Asia, and Africa meet, and every trade route of consequence passes through our domain. The dream of a universal Mediterranean commerce, governed from the Holy Land, has been realized. What legacy shall this achievement bear? Shall we become the pearl of the Orient, a naval power that commands the seas? Or the golden bridge between civilizations, a realm where learning and prosperity flow freely between all peoples?

options.text: Command the seas and all the world is ours.

modifiers.name: Pearl of the Orient
modifiers.text: The naval power of Jerusalem commands the eastern Mediterranean, its warships and merchantmen the masters of every sea lane.

options.text: Bridge the civilizations. Let learning flourish.

modifiers.name: Golden Bridge
modifiers.text: A cosmopolitan realm where the learning of East and West mingles freely, though the flood of wealth brings its own inflationary pressures.

units.name: Turcopoles
units.text: Locally recruited light cavalry serving as scouts, mounted archers, and skirmishers. Often drawn from Christianized Seljuks or Syrian Christians, they were indispensable to Crusader field armies.

units.name: Frankish Sergeants
units.text: Mounted men-at-arms who formed the backbone of Crusader field armies. Better equipped than common levies but not of knightly rank, they provided the steady infantry core of every engagement.

units.name: Outremer Galley
units.text: A war galley built and crewed in the ports of the Holy Land, adapted for the particular demands of Levantine coastal warfare and trade route protection.

units.name: Frankish Knights
units.text: The elite heavy cavalry of Outremer, armored knights mounted on powerful destriers, trained from youth in the arts of war and dedicated to the defense of the Holy Land.

buildings.name: Crusader Hall of Justice
buildings.text: A court of law administering the Assizes of Jerusalem, where the customs of the Frankish settlers are codified and applied to the governance of Outremer.

buildings.name: Concentric Fortress
buildings.text: A revolutionary multi-ring fortress with overlapping fields of fire, perfected by Crusader engineers in response to the advanced siege techniques of their Muslim adversaries.

buildings.name: Court of the Chain
buildings.text: The king's customs house and sea court in a port, named for the chain that closes the harbour of Acre. Every cargo landed is written down and taxed by its clerks, and its jurors judge the pleas of sailors and merchants. The Italian communes keep their own fondachi in the town; the Chain is where they must pay.

buildings.name: Pilgrim Workshop
buildings.text: A workshop of carvers in a town of the Holy Land. Rosaries, crosses and small models of the Holy Sepulchre are cut from olive wood and inlaid with mother of pearl.

buildings.name: Hospitaller Infirmary
buildings.text: A hospital built in the tradition of the Knights Hospitaller, where physicians trained in both European and Arabic medicine treat the sick and wounded.

buildings.name: Royal Palace of Jerusalem
buildings.text: The seat of the restored Crusader monarchy, a palace worthy of the ruler who holds the holiest city in Christendom.

buildings.name: Sugar Press
buildings.text: A mill for crushing the cane of a Crusader estate, with its boiling house beside it. An estate that can crush and boil its own cane plants more of it, and the land yields more sugar. The Levantine sugar trade was among the most profitable enterprises of the Latin kingdoms.

where.text: The location's raw material is Sugar

buildings.name: Bayyara
buildings.text: A walled orchard with its own well-house. A wheel lifts the water into a pool, and channels carry it to the trees through the dry months.

where.text: The location's raw material is Fruit

buildings.name: Church Militant
buildings.text: A fortified commandery of the military orders, half-church, half-fortress, where monks train as warriors and administer the conversion of conquered lands.

buildings.name: Eastern Exchange
buildings.text: A grand commercial exchange where merchants from three continents trade under one roof, a monument to the Kingdom of Jerusalem's position at the crossroads of the world.

list.name: Haute Cour
list.text: The High Court of Jerusalem, the feudal tribunal of the kingdom's tenants-in-chief. Constituted under Godfrey of Bouillon after 1099 and codified by John of Ibelin in the Livre des Assises de la Haute Cour around 1265, it heard cases involving the king's vassals, judged disputes over fiefs and homage, ratified successions, and (by the doctrine of conjuratio) could compel the king himself to honour the feudal contract on pain of release from homage. The Haute Cour was the constitutional engine of the Latin East: kings ruled by its consent, and the great baronial wars of the thirteenth century were fought in its name.

list.name: Cour des Bourgeois
list.text: The Burgesses' Court, the urban tribunal of the kingdom's Latin commoners. Codified in the Livre des Assises de la Cour des Bourgeois around 1240 (after a lost original of c. 1150), it had jurisdiction over property, debt, inheritance, and minor crimes among the burgensis class: artisans, merchants, sergeants, and pilgrim settlers. A jury of twelve burgesses sat under a royal viscount; commercial cases followed the Lex Mercatoria. Acre, Tyre, Jaffa, Caesarea, Nablus, and Jerusalem each had their own Cour des Bourgeois, distinct from the feudal Haute Cour above them.

list.name: Patriarchat Latin de Jerusalem
list.text: The Latin Patriarchate of Jerusalem, erected under Daimbert of Pisa in 1099 to replace the Greek hierarchy in the conquered Holy Sepulchre. The Patriarch held the Quarter of the Patriarch (a distinct urban jurisdiction in the holy city), administered the kingdom's tithe, and presided over ecclesiastical courts that drew jurisdiction over Frankish marriage and testament. After 1291 the see was preserved in titular form at Acre and later Cyprus. The Patriarchate was the spiritual counterweight to the Haute Cour and the legal bridge to Rome's canonical machinery.

list.name: Charte des Ordres Militaires
list.text: The royal charter governing the Templar, Hospitaller, and (later) Teutonic Orders within the kingdom. The military orders held vast estates (the Krak des Chevaliers, Margat, Atlit, Belvoir) outside ordinary feudal obligation, answered only to their Grand Masters and the Pope, and supplied the kingdom's most reliable standing armies. Their parallel administrative apparatus of commanderies, treasuries, and infirmaries ran a state-within-a-state; the charter defined what the orders owed the kingdom, and what they were exempt from.

list.name: Assises de Jerusalem
list.text: The codified feudal law of the kingdom, originally inscribed on the Lettres du Sepulcre kept in the Holy Sepulchre and lost when Saladin took Jerusalem in 1187. The corpus was reconstructed from memory by jurists in exile (John of Ibelin's Livre des Assises around 1265, Philip of Novara, James of Ibelin) and survived as the legal foundation of the kingdom of Cyprus and, in adapted form, the Assises de Romanie of Frankish Greece. The Assises codified the feudal contract, the criminal pleas of the king, and the jurisdiction of the kingdom's courts.
